page: Microsoft Azure D2 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The server is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs, providing 1.0 thread per core. It includes 7.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.5 GB of RAM per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA instruction sets. Local storage of 102 GB is bundled, and there are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the D2 instance in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance scored 1245.89 and multi-core scored 2442.49, both falling into the bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth tests showed 177.87 GB/sec for cached small blocks, while uncached large-block read and write bandwidths reached 23.29 GB/sec and 17.26 GB/sec respectively. Geekbench evaluations returned a single-core score of 1029.0 and a multi-core score of 1896.0, which ranks in the bottom 10%. Computational tasks such as software compilation with Clang scored 2571.0, while ray tracing and image processing benchmarks also registered in the lower percentiles.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation combined with modest memory and processing capabilities, this server represents an entry-level tier for workloads requiring predictable but low-intensity compute resources. The presence of 102 GB of local storage provides a baseline for local file caching or small database operations, though Passmark database operations of 1110.84 and Redis SET operations of 2.94 million operations per second indicate limited throughput. This configuration is suitable for basic web serving, lightweight background utilities, or development environments where high-throughput processing is not required.
